title: The 2011 report on dietary reference intakes for calcium and vitamin D from the Institute of Medicine: what clinicians need to know
authors: Ross AC, Manson JE, Abrams SA, Aloia JF, Brannon PM, Clinton SK, et al.
journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
funder: Institute of Medicine committee assembled at the request of agencies of the US and Canadian governments.
authorConflicts: None of the authors have conflicts of interest or other disclosures relevant to this publication.
result: Recommended Dietary Allowance of vitamin D 600 IU per day for ages 1 to 70 years and 800 IU per day from 71 years, corresponding to serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D of at least 20 ng/ml (50 nmol/l); tolerable upper intake level 4000 IU per day from 9 years. Evidence on cancer, cardiovascular disease, diabetes and autoimmune disorders was judged inconsistent, inconclusive as to causality and insufficient to set requirements.
